newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's "inside day" signals pullback.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's "inside day" signals pullback.

text.p: IPE Brent's failure on Wednesday to extend this week's rally and its subsequent "inside trading day" -- staying within its range on Tuesday -- signal a likely short-term technical retracement, chartists said.
But the most prophetic price action will come when and if Oct Brent, which settled at $22.11 a barrel, tests a gap left from Monday at $21.45 to $21, they said.
Filling the gap suggests it was an exhaustion gap that may confirm a top in the market, while staying above it would leave it a possible bullish breakaway gap, they added.

"The gap is still there but one has to admit the rise has been very over-extended and vulnerable to a correction given the acceleration we've seen in the market," said Susan Rigg, senior technical analyst at Chart Analysis.
"A move back below $21 is going to leave it vulnerable to a push to $20," she said.
Intraday support was pegged at its lows from the last three days at $21.65, $21.57 and the top of the gap at $21.45.
Oct Brent was expected to open 25 cents lower while Sept gas oil traded $2 lower at $205.50 a tonne at its 0815 GMT open.

Technical analysts noted that momentum indicators were at levels raising the odds for a correction. The 9- and 14-day Relative Strength Index levels were at 74 and 70 percent, respectively, coming into today.
One broker said crude's price action will hinge on gas oil and whether the Sept contract holds critical support at $200-201, which had been resistance the last five years.
"Around $201 is good support on gas oil and around $215 is resistance," he said.
He said energy prices normally trade back into a gap but that crude could hold up as long as gas oil stays above support.
Sept gas oil also left a gap from Monday at $201.50-199.50.

"The neutral stance is maintained, still looking for emerging evidence of a major top, still haven't found any," Al Graham, of Elliott Wave International in Gainesville, Georgia, said in his daily report.
"Weakness from $210.50 (basis October) to $197.75 can be labelled in the hourly chart as three down done," he said, using Elliott Wave analysis. "If so we go above $210.50 from $197.75."
He said exceeding resistance at $205.75, a Fibonacci retracement level, with support holding at $197.75 reinforces the chances for a move to $210.50.

He warned that "we're near a major top, but there is still no evidence that a top is in place." And despite a sharp drop from its high of $210.50 to Tuesday's close, he said price action using wave analysis was "not yet unmistakably impulsive, and that leaves the door open for another high."
Support for Oct is the top of its gap at $196.25, he said.
Oct traded $1.75 lower at $200.50 early Thursday.
